# Mega evolution in MAG — a spec for the refit

**Version 3.61.0 · 2026-08-06**

**Every figure here is generated by `engine/mega_decision_census.js` into `data/mega-decision.json`.**
Nothing is typed. Two hand-typed store counts in `docs/GAME-DIFFERENTIAL-DESIGN.md` had already drifted
apart from each other and from the file within hours of being written, and the census exists so this
document cannot repeat it.

---

## 1. Where this came from

Will, 2026-08-06: *"WHAT IF WE ADD MEGA EVOLUTION TO THE MAG WEIGHTS"*, then two proposed features —
*"SO IF MEGA I OUTSPEED"* and *"IF MEGA I GAIN WEATHER CONTROL"* — and then the constraint that
reorganises the whole design:

> *"although it needs to be a separate score than from the move selection or switching because you can
> mega and act at the same turn"*

**That constraint is correct and it is not a detail.** MAG is a conditional logit over a choice set:
`P(pick j) = exp(w·x_j) / Σ exp(w·x_k)`. A softmax assumes you pick **one**. Mega is not one of the
options — **you mega AND you act**. Adding a `mega` row to the choice set would model the player as
choosing mega *instead of* clicking Flare Blitz, which is not the game.

---

## 2. The three preconditions, measured

A feature fitted on human clicks needs the decision to be **observed**, **timed**, and **variable**.
All three are asked by the census rather than assumed.

| | raw ladder store | clean corpus |
|---|---:|---:|
| games | 47,210 | 8,493 |
| games with ≥1 mega | **93.1%** | **98.53%** |
| both sides megaed | 61.32% | 78.54% |
| mega events | 74,944 | **15,803** |
| share executed on **turn 1** | 47.78% | **40.47%** |

**Observed:** yes. **15,803 mega events in the clean corpus** — the number that matters, because
anything about *judgement* must be fitted on games not dominated by bots. (An earlier statement in
conversation put this at 74,944; that is the RAW figure and it is the wrong one to quote for a fit.)

**Timed:** yes, and more so once the corpus is cleaned. **59.53% of clean megas are held past turn 1.**
If this were ~100% on turn 1 there would be no decision to fit and ROADMAP #31's *"today it is a
default — the lead keeps it"* would be a harmless simplification. It is not.

**Variable:** yes, and the shape is narrower than it first appears — see §3.

---

## 3. What megaing actually buys, across 98 mega formes

| | count of 98 |
|---|---:|
| gain base Speed | 61 |
| gain **no** Speed at all | **26** |
| **set weather** on evolving | **4** |
| conditional speed **ability** | **1** |
| ability **not** overwritten | 21 |

**Three corrections to what was said in conversation before this was measured:**

- **Weather is 4 formes, not a family** — `charizardmegay`→sun, `tyranitarmega`→sand,
  `abomasnowmega`→snow, `froslassmega`→snow. It matters by **usage**, not by breadth: Charizard-Mega-Y
  is the single most-used mega in the store.
- **Conditional speed abilities are ONE forme** — `swampertmega`, Swift Swim, ×2 in rain. It was
  described as a group; it is not.
- **Charizard-Mega-Y gains ZERO base Speed**, and so does Charizard-Mega-X. The most-used mega in the
  format is a counter-example to *"if mega I outspeed"*. The largest gains are `absolmegaz` +76,
  `beedrillmega` +70, `lucariomegaz` +61 — none of which was the example reached for from memory.

**This variation is the whole argument for a weight rather than a rule.** Blastoise-Mega gains no
Speed and sets no weather; Absol-Mega gains 76. *"Mega is good"* is false as a rule and estimable as a
conditional weight.

---

## 4. The design, given that you mega AND act

Three options were considered. **The first is wrong for the reason in §1** and is recorded so it is not
re-proposed.

### ✗ 4a. Add `mega` as a row in the choice set
Models mega as competing with your move. It does not. Rejected.

### ✓ 4b. Mega is a BOARD TRANSFORMATION; score the same moves twice
The action space is a **product**, not a union: `(mega? × move × target)`.

```
score(mega=no,  m) = MAG(m)  evaluated on the CURRENT board
score(mega=yes, m) = MAG(m)  evaluated on the POST-MEGA board
```

**This is why almost nothing new needs to be written.** "If mega I outspeed" is not a feature — it is
`movesFirst`, recomputed on a board where the Speed stat is different. "If mega I gain weather control"
is not a feature — it is the existing weather-dependent features, recomputed on a board where sun is up.
**The existing 58 already say these things; they have simply never been offered the post-mega board.**

That also sidesteps ROADMAP #79's admission rule for most of it: a re-scored existing feature needs no
new justification, where a new column would have to earn its place on held-out likelihood.

**Cost: the candidate set doubles**, ~64 pairs → ~128, for the one Pokémon that can still evolve. That
is a speed budget question (#76, #61), and it is the reason this is a spec rather than a patch.

### ✓ 4c. One genuinely new thing — the resource
Re-scoring on the transformed board captures everything about **this** turn and nothing about the
**cost**. The mega is once per battle. Spending it now forecloses spending it on turn 4, and no
re-scored feature can see that, because every feature MAG has is about the present board.

So the new columns are small and are about the *option*, not the *effect*:

| candidate | says |
|---|---|
| `megaSpent` | this action consumes the side's one mega |
| `megaUrgency` | the body holding the stone is at risk of fainting before it can be spent |

`megaUrgency` is Will's own question from 2026-08-06 — *"how many of the raichus and all these megas
died before they could evolve?"* — and it is the honest form of the resource cost: the option is worth
less when it may expire.

---

## 5. What this can and cannot decide

**MAG can learn WHEN A HUMAN MEGAS. It cannot tell you whether megaing is CORRECT.**

MAG is behaviour cloning (`docs/GLOSSARY.md` §3) and caps at its target by construction. A once-per-
battle resource is valued by what it is worth *later*, which is a position-and-future question, not an
action-on-this-board question. That is `CLAUDE.md`'s rule that features are per-model: MAG scores an
ACTION, a value function scores a POSITION.

- **MAG + mega** → a better opponent model (*will they mega this turn?*), a better prior, better
  pruning. Directly useful, and currently **absent entirely** for a decision present in 98.53% of clean
  games.
- **Whether WE mega** → search and the value function. **ROADMAP #31's engine half landed in 3.61.0;
  the DECISION half — a search that chooses whether to spend the mega — has not.** Not this spec's job.

---

## 6. Preconditions before any of this is fitted

1. ~~**The engine must be able to represent the decision.**~~ **DONE, 3.61.0.** MEDICHAM megaed at
   BUILD time, so there was no post-mega board to score against and no mega action to fit. ROADMAP #31
   landed: evolution is a choice taken mid-turn, every offered choice is taken identically by both
   engines, and the differential now tests mega bodies with no stone stripped. **The post-mega board
   §4b needs now exists.**
2. **Fitting environment must match playing environment** (`CLAUDE.md`). Weights fitted with mega as a
   build-time fact are not valid for an engine that megas on a choice. This lands **with** the refit,
   not before it.
3. **ROADMAP #79's admission rule applies to §4c only.** `megaSpent` and `megaUrgency` each have to
   improve held-out likelihood against the set without them, or they do not ship. The §4b re-scoring is
   not a new feature and is not subject to it.
4. **The censoring caveat travels with any fit.** The store records a mega that HAPPENED. It cannot
   record one that was considered and held, nor one whose body fainted before it could be spent. The
   turn-share is therefore a distribution over **executed** megas and a **lower bound** on how often the
   decision was faced. This is stated in `data/mega-decision.json`'s own `caveat` field.
